results.name: rule_member_above_max_yes
results.description: Among sets of 2+ distinct examples all fitting a rule with <=20 members (squares, cubes, powers, multiples of 5-12, ends in d), yes rate on targets in the smallest such rule that lie above the largest example; observed above null means the model's ratio ceiling wrongly suppresses rule-based upward extrapolation (below null = ceiling too lenient for rules).

results.name: overshoot_by_set_size_gap
results.description: Yes rate on targets just above the largest example (max < target <= 1.5*max) for 1-example sets minus for 3-4-example sets; observed above null means the ceiling should tighten more with the number of examples than the model's set-size-independent ratio ceiling allows (below null = less).
results.code:
# name: overshoot_by_set_size_gap
# description: Yes rate on targets just above the largest example (max < target <= 1.5*max) for 1-example sets minus for 3-4-example sets; observed above null means the ceiling should tighten more with the number of examples than the model's set-size-independent ratio ceiling allows (below null = less).
def test_statistic(df):
    info = {}
    for s in df["number_set"].astype(str).unique():
        ex = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        info[s] = (len(ex), max(ex))
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    k = np.array([info[s][0] for s in ns])
    mx = np.array([info[s][1] for s in ns]).astype(float)
    tg = df["target"].astype(int).values
    over = (tg > mx) & (tg <= 1.5 * mx)
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    a = over & (k == 1)
    b = over & (k >= 3)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: new_set_gap_by_set_size
results.description: (First-query minus repeat-query yes rate on non-example targets) for 1-2-example sets minus the same gap for 3-4-example sets; nonzero vs null means the new-set criterion shift depends on set size, which the model's single constant shift cannot capture (positive = small sets show a more liberal/less cautious first query relative to large sets).
results.code:
# name: new_set_gap_by_set_size
# description: (First-query minus repeat-query yes rate on non-example targets) for 1-2-example sets minus the same gap for 3-4-example sets; nonzero vs null means the new-set criterion shift depends on set size, which the model's single constant shift cannot capture (positive = small sets show a more liberal/less cautious first query relative to large sets).
def test_statistic(df):
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    ti = df["trial_index"].values
    prev = np.concatenate([[""], ns[:-1]])
    first = (ns != prev) | (ti == 0)
    k = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.count(",").values + 1
    tgt = df["target"].astype(int).astype(str).values
    is_ex = np.array([t in s.split(",") for s, t in zip(ns, tgt)])
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    def gap(mask):
        a = mask & first & ~is_ex
        b = mask & ~first & ~is_ex
        if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
            return 0.0
        return r[a].mean() - r[b].mean()
    return float(gap(k <= 2) - gap(k >= 3))

results.name: block_position_late_minus_second
results.description: Within runs of consecutive trials with the same set, yes rate on non-example targets at run position >= 3 (third query onward) minus at position 2 (second query); observed above null means willingness to say "yes" keeps growing with repeated queries about a set, beyond the model's single first-trial shift (below null = it decays).
results.code:
# name: block_position_late_minus_second
# description: Within runs of consecutive trials with the same set, yes rate on non-example targets at run position >= 3 (third query onward) minus at position 2 (second query); observed above null means willingness to say "yes" keeps growing with repeated queries about a set, beyond the model's single first-trial shift (below null = it decays).
def test_statistic(df):
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    ti = df["trial_index"].values
    prev = np.concatenate([[""], ns[:-1]])
    first = (ns != prev) | (ti == 0)
    blk = np.cumsum(first)
    pos = pd.Series(np.zeros(len(df))).groupby(blk).cumcount().values
    tgt = df["target"].astype(int).astype(str).values
    is_ex = np.array([t in s.split(",") for s, t in zip(ns, tgt)])
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    a = (pos >= 2) & ~is_ex
    b = (pos == 1) & ~is_ex
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: new_set_overlap_first_trial_gap
results.description: On the first trial after a set change (non-example targets, trial_index > 0), yes rate when the new set shares at least one example with the previous trial's set minus when it shares none; observed above null means overlapping sets are treated as continuations (less new-set caution or carried-over belief), which the model's uniform first-trial shift misses.
results.code:
# name: new_set_overlap_first_trial_gap
# description: On the first trial after a set change (non-example targets, trial_index > 0), yes rate when the new set shares at least one example with the previous trial's set minus when it shares none; observed above null means overlapping sets are treated as continuations (less new-set caution or carried-over belief), which the model's uniform first-trial shift misses.
def test_statistic(df):
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    ti = df["trial_index"].values
    prev = np.concatenate([[""], ns[:-1]])
    first = (ns != prev) & (ti > 0)
    tgt = df["target"].astype(int).astype(str).values
    is_ex = np.array([t in s.split(",") for s, t in zip(ns, tgt)])
    ov = np.array([bool(set(a.split(",")) & set(b.split(","))) for a, b in zip(ns, prev)])
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    a = first & ov & ~is_ex
    b = first & ~ov & ~is_ex
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: narrow_vs_wide_range_inside_gap
results.description: For sets of 2+ distinct examples, yes rate on non-example targets strictly inside [min, max] that share no final digit with any example, for sets with range <= 25 minus sets with range >= 60; observed above null means people fill in narrow clusters more (or wide spans less) than the model's interval/run account predicts.
results.code:
# name: narrow_vs_wide_range_inside_gap
# description: For sets of 2+ distinct examples, yes rate on non-example targets strictly inside [min, max] that share no final digit with any example, for sets with range <= 25 minus sets with range >= 60; observed above null means people fill in narrow clusters more (or wide spans less) than the model's interval/run account predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    info = {}
    for s in df["number_set"].astype(str).unique():
        ex = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        info[s] = (len(set(ex)), min(ex), max(ex), set(x % 10 for x in ex), set(ex))
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    tg = df["target"].astype(int).values
    k = np.array([info[s][0] for s in ns])
    mn = np.array([info[s][1] for s in ns])
    mx = np.array([info[s][2] for s in ns])
    ok = np.array([(t % 10) not in info[s][3] and t not in info[s][4] for s, t in zip(ns, tg)])
    inside = (k >= 2) & (tg > mn) & (tg < mx) & ok
    rng = mx - mn
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    a = inside & (rng <= 25)
    b = inside & (rng >= 60)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: cross_set_carryover
results.description: On the first trial after the set changes (excluding session start and trials repeating the previous target), P(yes | previous trial yes) minus P(yes | previous trial no) within a session; observed above null means a response perseveration/momentum across sets that the model (independent trials) under-produces.
results.code:
# name: cross_set_carryover
# description: On the first trial after the set changes (excluding session start and trials repeating the previous target), P(yes | previous trial yes) minus P(yes | previous trial no) within a session; observed above null means a response perseveration/momentum across sets that the model (independent trials) under-produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    ti = df["trial_index"].values
    tg = df["target"].values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    prev_ns = np.concatenate([[""], ns[:-1]])
    prev_r = np.concatenate([[np.nan], r[:-1]])
    prev_t = np.concatenate([[-1], tg[:-1]])
    m = (ns != prev_ns) & (ti > 0) & (tg != prev_t)
    a = m & (prev_r == 1)
    b = m & (prev_r == 0)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: just_below_min_yes_rate
results.description: Among sets of 2+ examples whose smallest example is >= 20, yes rate on targets 1-15 below the smallest example; observed above null means the model (ceiling above, but no graded floor below) under-produces downward extension near the minimum (below null = people impose a floor the model lacks).
